x: Sound intensity level is measured in decibels (dB). Knot is a speed unit, ampere is current and candela is luminous intensity.
Momentum = mass × velocity, with unit kg m/s, which equals newton second (N·s), since 1 N = 1 kg m/s².
source: NextGen Rocket Physics (src/science-tech/rocket-physics.txt) p.10-11; NCERT Science (standard textbook fact, not in the local library)

x: Stress is force per unit area, so it has the same unit as pressure (pascal, N/m²). Strain is dimensionless.
Resistivity ρ = RA/l, so its unit is ohm × length: ohm-metre in SI, ohm-cm in CGS. Ohm is the unit of resistance itself.
source: NextGen Rocket Physics (src/science-tech/rocket-physics.txt) p.44 (resistivity Ω m / Ω cm)

x: Joule, watt-hour and newton-metre are all units of energy. Kg·m/s² is the unit of force (newton), so it is not an energy unit.
Momentum = mass × velocity, so its SI unit is kg m s⁻¹.
The newton is the SI unit of force. The other options are units of pressure (pascal), power (watt) and energy (joule).
The henry (H) is the SI unit of inductance.
Resistivity ρ = RA/l, so its SI unit is the ohm-metre (Ω m). Tesla is magnetic field; V/m is electric field.
source: NextGen Rocket Physics (src/science-tech/rocket-physics.txt) p.44; PMF General Science Part 6 (src/science-tech/pmf-general-science-06.txt)

x: Torque = force × perpendicular distance, so its unit is N m. Force is in N, power in W and acceleration in m/s².
source: NextGen Rocket Physics (src/science-tech/rocket-physics.txt) p.15; NCERT Science (standard textbook fact, not in the local library)
